# When does joint reconciliation matter? {#sec-theory}

## Joint and separate reconciliation

Stack the $m$ variables as in ([-@eq-vec]), with summing matrix $\bm{S}_*$ and constraint matrix $\bm{C}_*$.
Let $\bm{W}$ be the $(mn \times mn)$ covariance matrix of the stacked base forecast errors $\bm{e} = (\bm{e}_1', \dots, \bm{e}_m')'$, where $\bm{e}_j$ holds the $n$ errors of variable $j$, and write $\bm{W}_{jk} = \cov(\bm{e}_j, \bm{e}_k)$ for its $(n \times n)$ blocks.
We drop the horizon subscript $h$ throughout this section.

Joint MinT reconciliation in zero-constrained form [@di2023cross] is $\widetilde{\bm{y}} = \bm{M}\widehat{\bm{y}}$ with
$$
  \bm{M} = \bm{I} - \bm{L}\bm{C}_*,
  \qquad
  \bm{L} = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'(\bm{C}_*\bm{W}\bm{C}_*')^{-1}.
$$ {#eq-joint-map}
Separate reconciliation applies univariate MinT to each variable using its own error covariance $\bm{W}_{jj}$.
Its map is block diagonal, $\bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}} = \operatorname{diag}(\bm{M}_1, \dots, \bm{M}_m)$, with
$$
  \bm{M}_j = \bm{I} - \bm{L}_j\bm{C},
  \qquad
  \bm{L}_j = \bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'(\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}')^{-1}.
$$ {#eq-sep-map}

Both maps have a regression interpretation.
The incoherence of the base forecasts, $\bm{C}_*\widehat{\bm{y}} = -\bm{C}_*\bm{e}$, is observable, and $\bm{L}$ is the matrix of population regression coefficients of the errors $\bm{e}$ on the incoherences $\bm{C}_*\bm{e}$, since $\cov(\bm{e}, \bm{C}_*\bm{e}) = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$.
MinT adds the fitted value of this regression, an estimate of the base forecast error computed from the observed incoherences, to the base forecasts: $\widetilde{\bm{y}} = \widehat{\bm{y}} + \bm{L}\bm{C}_*\bm{e}$.
Separate reconciliation runs the same regression for each variable, using only its own incoherences $\bm{C}\bm{e}_j$.
The off-diagonal blocks of $\bm{L}$ are the coefficients on the other variables' incoherences, and joint reconciliation can only improve on separate reconciliation through them.

## When joint and separate reconciliation coincide

::: {#prp-equivalence}
Let $\bm{W}$ be positive definite.
The following statements are equivalent.

(a) $\bm{M} = \bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}}$: joint and separate reconciliation give the same forecasts for every base forecast.
(b) $\bm{M}$ is block diagonal by variable.
(c) $\bm{L}$ is block diagonal by variable.
(d) $\bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{0}$ for all $j \ne k$; that is, $\cov(\bm{M}_j\bm{e}_j, \bm{C}\bm{e}_k) = \bm{0}$.
(e) The column space of $\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$ is contained in that of $\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'$ for all $j \ne k$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Let $\bm{Q} = \bm{C}_*\bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$, with blocks $\bm{Q}_{jk} = \bm{C}\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$.
Because $\bm{W}$ is positive definite and $\bm{C}_*$ has full row rank, $\bm{Q}$ is invertible, so $\bm{L}$ is the unique solution of $\bm{L}\bm{Q} = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$.
Block $(j,k)$ of the right-hand side is $\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$.

(c)$\Rightarrow$(a).
Let $\bm{L} = \operatorname{diag}(\bm{H}_1, \dots, \bm{H}_m)$.
Block $(j,j)$ of $\bm{L}\bm{Q} = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$ gives $\bm{H}_j\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}' = \bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'$, so $\bm{H}_j = \bm{L}_j$.
Hence $\bm{M} = \bm{I} - \bm{L}\bm{C}_* = \operatorname{diag}(\bm{I} - \bm{L}_j\bm{C}) = \bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}}$.

(a)$\Rightarrow$(b) is immediate.

(b)$\Rightarrow$(c).
$\bm{L}\bm{C}_* = \bm{I} - \bm{M}$ is block diagonal.
Since $\bm{C}_*$ is block diagonal with full row rank, it has the block diagonal right inverse $\bm{C}_*'(\bm{C}_*\bm{C}_*')^{-1}$, and $\bm{L} = (\bm{L}\bm{C}_*)\bm{C}_*'(\bm{C}_*\bm{C}_*')^{-1}$ is block diagonal.

(c)$\Leftrightarrow$(d).
By the argument for (c)$\Rightarrow$(a), $\bm{L}$ is block diagonal if and only if $\bm{L} = \bm{L}^{\mathrm{sep}} = \operatorname{diag}(\bm{L}_1, \dots, \bm{L}_m)$.
By uniqueness, this holds if and only if $\bm{L}^{\mathrm{sep}}\bm{Q} = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$.
Blocks $(j,j)$ of this equation hold by the definition of $\bm{L}_j$.
Blocks $(j,k)$ with $j \ne k$ read $\bm{L}_j\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$, that is, $(\bm{I} - \bm{L}_j\bm{C})\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{0}$.
Finally, $\cov(\bm{M}_j\bm{e}_j, \bm{C}\bm{e}_k) = \bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$.

(d)$\Leftrightarrow$(e).
Condition (d) states $\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'\bm{D}_{jk}$ with $\bm{D}_{jk} = (\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}')^{-1}\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}'$, so (d) implies (e).
Conversely, if $\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'\bm{D}$ for some $\bm{D}$, then $\bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = \bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'\bm{D} = \bm{0}$, because $\bm{M}_j\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}' = \bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}' - \bm{L}_j\bm{C}\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}' = \bm{0}$.
:::

Condition (d) has a direct reading.
Joint reconciliation changes nothing if and only if, after each variable has been reconciled on its own, its remaining errors are uncorrelated with the incoherences of every other variable.
Condition (b) shows that there is no intermediate case.
If the reconciled forecasts of one variable depend on the base forecasts of another at all, they differ from the separately reconciled forecasts.

Two known results are special cases of @prp-equivalence.

::: {#cor-invariance name="Invariance"}
For any $\bm{K}$ such that $\bm{W} + \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*'$ is positive definite, replacing $\bm{W}$ by $\bm{W} + \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*'$ leaves $\bm{M}$, $\bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $\bm{L}$ unchanged.
:::

::: {.proof}
Since $\bm{C}\bm{S} = \bm{0}$, we have $\bm{C}_*\bm{S}_* = \bm{0}$, so $(\bm{W} + \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*')\bm{C}_*' = \bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$ and $\bm{C}_*(\bm{W} + \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*')\bm{C}_*' = \bm{C}_*\bm{W}\bm{C}_*'$.
Hence $\bm{L}$, and so $\bm{M}$, is unchanged.
The diagonal blocks change by $\bm{S}\bm{K}_{jj}\bm{S}'$, which leaves each $\bm{L}_j$, and so $\bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}}$, unchanged by the same argument.
:::

This is the argument used by @wickramasuriya2021properties [Proposition 1] to show that the GLS reconciliation of @hyndman2011optimal and MinT coincide.
It is an instance of the classical result that generalised least squares is unaffected by adding $\bm{X}\bm{K}\bm{X}'$ to the error covariance, where $\bm{X}$ is the regressor matrix [@rao1967least; @zyskind1967canonical].
Only the part of the error covariance that is visible through the incoherences matters.
Any cross-variable dependence of the form $\bm{S}\bm{K}_{jk}\bm{S}'$ is invisible to both joint and separate reconciliation.
The same invariance gives the known condition $\bm{W} = \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*' + \tau\bm{I}$ under which MinT reduces to OLS reconciliation [@hyndman2011optimal; @wickramasuriya2021properties].

::: {#cor-separable name="Separability"}
If $\bm{W} = \bm{V} \otimes \bm{\Sigma}_0$ for positive definite matrices $\bm{V}$ $(m \times m)$ and $\bm{\Sigma}_0$ $(n \times n)$, then $\bm{M} = \bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}} = \bm{I}_m \otimes \bm{M}_0$, where $\bm{M}_0 = \bm{I} - \bm{\Sigma}_0\bm{C}'(\bm{C}\bm{\Sigma}_0\bm{C}')^{-1}\bm{C}$, whatever the sign or strength of the cross-variable dependence in $\bm{V}$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Here $\bm{W}_{jk} = v_{jk}\bm{\Sigma}_0$, so $\bm{L}_j = \bm{\Sigma}_0\bm{C}'(\bm{C}\bm{\Sigma}_0\bm{C}')^{-1}$ and $\bm{M}_j = \bm{M}_0$ for every $j$.
Then $\bm{W}_{jk}\bm{C}' = (v_{jk}/v_{jj})\bm{W}_{jj}\bm{C}'$, and condition (e) holds.
:::

@cor-separable is a special case of a result of @girolimetto2025cross for cross-temporal reconciliation in which the second dimension carries no aggregation constraints.
It is the reconciliation analogue of the result that seemingly unrelated regressions with identical regressors reduce to equation-by-equation least squares [@zellner1962efficient]: every variable shares the same summing matrix, so cross-variable correlation alone cannot be exploited.
Corollaries [-@cor-invariance] and [-@cor-separable] combine: every $\bm{W} = \bm{V} \otimes \bm{\Sigma}_0 + \bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*'$ satisfies the conditions of @prp-equivalence, however far it is from a Kronecker product.
So separability is sufficient but far from necessary.

This limits the value of measuring separability directly.
If $\bm{W}$ is rearranged so that each block $\bm{W}_{jk}$ becomes a row, it is a Kronecker product if and only if the rearranged matrix has rank one, and the relative error of the nearest Kronecker approximation [@vanloan1993approximation] is $\{1 - \sigma_1^2/\sum_i\sigma_i^2\}^{1/2}$, where $\sigma_i$ are the singular values of the rearranged matrix.
Likelihood ratio tests of separability are also available [@lu2005likelihood; @mitchell2006likelihood].
Both measures of separability respond to components $\bm{S}_*\bm{K}\bm{S}_*'$ that do not change the reconciled forecasts, and a departure that does change them may leave the Kronecker error small.

## Remarks

*Horizon.* Under the usual simplifying assumption $\bm{W}_h = k_h\bm{W}_1$, the maps $\bm{M}$ and $\bm{M}^{\mathrm{sep}}$ do not depend on $h$, and neither do the conditions of @prp-equivalence.

*Shrinkage.* The diagonal target of the shrinkage estimator has zero cross-variable blocks and so satisfies condition (d).
Full shrinkage therefore makes joint reconciliation identical to reconciling each variable separately with its own diagonal target, and partial shrinkage scales the estimated cross-variable blocks of $\bm{W}$ towards zero.

*Linear combinations.* MinT minimises not only the trace of the reconciled error covariance but the whole matrix in the positive semidefinite order, since it is the generalised least squares projection [@wickramasuriya2019optimal].
Separate reconciliation is another linear reconciliation of this form (its $\bm{G}$ satisfies $\bm{G}\bm{S}_* = \bm{I}$), so for every linear combination $\bm{\ell}'\bm{y}$ of the stacked series, such as the difference between two variables at one node, joint reconciliation with the true $\bm{W}$ has no larger error variance.
When the conditions of @prp-equivalence fail, the gain need not be spread evenly: it can be negligible for each variable's own series yet substantial for combinations that load on several variables.

*More than two variables.* @prp-equivalence holds for any $m$, and condition (d) can be checked pair by pair.
Joint reconciliation of $m$ variables can be split into separate reconciliations of groups of variables whenever the off-diagonal blocks of $\bm{L}$ between groups vanish.
